1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2	
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4	
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6	
7	- **Install**:
8	  - macOS — Homebrew (`herdr` is in homebrew-core; managed by the `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
9	  - Linux — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr` (managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in the same role). No tarball, so no unarchive step.
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: brew on macOS; `herdr update` for the self-managed Linux binary
12	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **seed-once** (`dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml`, the `create_` prefix). herdr writes UI settings back into this file (see [Config writeback](#config-writeback-why-create_)), so chezmoi plants it on a fresh machine and then never touches it.
13	
14	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Model differences vs tmux
19	
20	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** (tmux is Session → Window → Pane). "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
21	
22	## Feasibility matrix (current tmux experience → herdr)
23	
24	| Current capability | herdr story | How it's handled here |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| Catppuccin theme + light/dark | **Native** `[theme]` + `auto_switch` | Configured in `config.toml` |
27	| Splits / zoom / new tab+workspace / pane nav | **Native** `[keys]` actions | Rebound to tmux muscle memory |
28	| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
29	| Mouse / right-click menus | **Native** mouse-first | Skipped — native |
30	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux) |
31	| `sesh` fuzzy switch + `tmuxp` layouts | **Plugin** [herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) Projects + Quick Actions | Plugin + Projects templates |
32	| `tv` channel popups (`prefix+T/U/a`) | **Custom command panes** (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) | Key bindings + 2 herdr-aware channels |
33	| lazygit / scratch popups | **Custom command panes** | Key bindings |
34	| Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane nav | **No herdr-aware smart-splits** | **Gap** — workaround below |
35	| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
36	| Per-window status glyphs + bookmarks ⭐📌 | **No format-string interpolation** | **Gap** — native agent dots replace the agent part |
37	| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
38	
39	## Keybindings
40	
41	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
42	
43	| Key | Action | Type |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
46	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
47	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + minus` | split side-by-side / stacked | rebound |
48	| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
49	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace nav / session navigator | built-in default |
50	| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
51	| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
52	| `prefix + ?` | keybinds help overlay — lists every active binding with labels (herdr's native which-key; manually invoked, not an auto-timeout hint) | built-in default |
53	| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
54	| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
55	| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
56	| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
57	| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
58	| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
59	| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
60	| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
61	| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
62	| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
63	| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |
64	
65	> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
66	
67	## Session helpers: `hvibe` / `hcode` (herdr analogs of `svibe` / `scode`)
68	
69	Two shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) spin up a whole coding workspace in one motion — the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` helpers. They shell out to the native `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI and **reuse svibe's pure logic verbatim** (specstory wrapping, `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`, git-root resolution, agent-CLI detection) from `22_sesh.sh`; only the layout calls differ. Need the `herdr` server running + `jq`.
70	
71	| Command | Builds workspace | Layout |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| `hvibe [N] [CLI]` / `hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode` | `vibe/<repo>` | tab `agents` (N even-width agent panes) + tab `git` (lazygit) + tab `edit` (nvim) |
74	| `hvibe --tab-per-agent …` | `vibe/<repo>` | one tab **per agent** + `git` + `edit` tabs |
75	| `hcode [CLI]` | `coding-agent/<repo>` | tab `editor` (nvim 75% \| agent 25%) + tab `monitor` (btop) |
76	
77	- **Idempotent per repo**: re-running focuses the existing `vibe/<repo>` / `coding-agent/<repo>` workspace instead of duplicating (matches svibe's "attach if exists").
78	- **Agent visibility**: herdr tracks agent state **per pane**, so in the default splits layout every agent still surfaces individually in herdr's agent tracking (verified: two agents in one tab appear as two separate entries in `herdr agent list`). The compact left sidebar rolls a *tab's* status into one dot — use `--tab-per-agent` if you want each agent to own a tab-level status dot.
79	- **Even columns**: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so `hvibe` sets each split's `--ratio` explicitly (`1/(N-m+1)`) to keep the agent panes even; `hcode` uses `--ratio 0.75` to give nvim 75%.
80	- Same flags as svibe/scode: `--on-exit`, `--no-specstory`, `--no-attach`, `-p/--path`; `hvibe` also takes `--min-width` / `--tab-per-agent` and honors `$HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH` / `$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER`. Full flag help: `hvibe -h` / `hcode -h`.
81	
82	The tmux `svibe` / `scode` remain the tmux-side equivalents (see [sesh](sesh.md)); the two families coexist — `hvibe`/`hcode` only touch herdr, `svibe`/`scode` only touch tmux.
83	
84	## herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + menu analog)
85	
86	[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) adds **Projects** (declarative multi-tab/multi-pane workspace templates with a fuzzy picker — the `tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` analog) and **Quick Actions** (a fuzzy command launcher — the popup-menu analog).
87	
88	**Install is automated** by the `devtools` ansible role (the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block) — idempotent, runs on every `chezmoi apply`, skipped once installed. It shells out to:
89	
90	```bash
91	herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus   # manual fallback / what the role runs
92	```
93	
94	`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The one trap: if a *stale* Go is on `PATH` (e.g. an old `/usr/local/go` shadowing a newer one) herdr tries to build from source and fails (`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`) instead of falling back. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. (Go is mise-managed now, gated on `installExtraRuntimes`.)
95	
96	Project templates are chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → the same path under `~/.config/`. The shipped `chezmoi.toml` mirrors this repo's tmuxinator `chezmoi` session (editor/git/shell tabs). Bind `prefix+O` → Projects and `prefix+y` → Quick Actions (already in the config).
97	
98	## Television integration
99	
100	Most `tv` channels (`tools`, `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `kill-process`, `ssh-config`) have **non-tmux-coupled actions**, so they run unchanged in a herdr command pane — just bind a key to `tv <channel>`. Only the channels whose actions call `tmux …` need herdr-aware variants. Two ship here:
101	
102	- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`.
103	- `herdr-agent-panes` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml`) — same source as `agent-panes`, but switch/kill use `herdr pane focus` / `herdr pane close`.
104	
105	The original tmux-bound `sesh` / `agent-panes` channels are left intact for coexistence.
106	
107	## Agent state (replaces the 6-file workmux integration)
108	
109	herdr detects agent state natively and rolls it up into the sidebar (a blocked agent marks its pane/tab/workspace). Claude Code is detected via **screen-manifest heuristics** (terminal title + OSC progress), not lifecycle hooks. If the heuristics prove insufficient, state can be pushed explicitly:
110	
111	```bash
112	herdr pane report-agent w1:p1 --agent claude --state working
113	```
114	
115	For the trial we rely on native detection — the tmux-side workmux 🤖/💬/✅ system (Claude/OpenCode hooks → `@workmux_status`) is untouched and only applies under tmux.
116	
117	### Optional agent integrations (the onboarding "install" button)
118	
119	herdr's first-run onboarding offers to **install optional agent integrations** (`herdr integration install <agent>`), so agents report state directly instead of relying on screen heuristics. Pressing *install* sets these up for every detected agent. What it writes (verified on this machine):
120	
121	| Agent | What `herdr integration install` creates | Touches a repo-managed file? |
122	|---|---|---|
123	| claude | `~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh` **+ a hook entry in `~/.claude/settings.json`** | Yes — but the repo's hook-aware `modify_settings.json` merger **preserves** it (same as it does for CodeIsland). `chezmoi apply` is a no-op; it won't strip the herdr hook. |
124	| codex | `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh` only | No — `~/.codex/config.toml` is untouched (identical to the chezmoi-computed target). |
125	| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js` (separate plugin) | No — only `workmux-status.ts` is managed; herdr's plugin coexists. |
126	| cursor | `~/.cursor/herdr-agent-state.sh` + hook | Script lives outside chezmoi; coexists. |
127	
128	These integration files are **not** vendored into the repo, so they do **not** reproduce on other machines (press *install* again there, or skip onboarding). They use herdr's own socket and do not interfere with tmux/workmux (different mechanism). To remove: `herdr integration uninstall <agent>` — and for **claude**, rerun `chezmoi apply` afterwards so the merger drops the now-removed hook from `settings.json`.
129	
130	### Config writeback (why `create_`)
131	
132	herdr **writes UI/runtime settings back into `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`** — e.g. finishing onboarding prepends `onboarding = false`, and the in-app *settings* popups (theme / sound / toasts / pane labels) persist there on *apply*. It edits in place and keeps existing comments, but it owns the file at runtime. That is why chezmoi manages it as **`create_` (seed-once)**: a plain managed file would be clobbered on every `chezmoi apply` (re-removing `onboarding=false` → the onboarding screen reappears, and reverting any UI change). Consequence: edits to `create_config.toml` in the repo do **not** auto-propagate to a machine that already has the file — refresh it deliberately with `cp ~/.config/herdr/config.toml "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/herdr/config.toml)"` (then strip the runtime `onboarding`/state lines).
133	
134	## Persistence & restore (accidental close)
135	
136	Two native layers, no plugin needed:
137	
138	- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
139	- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
140	
141	## AI usage / quota status
142	
143	herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into. A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
144	
145	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
146	
147	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
148	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
149	- **Status-bar format glyphs + bookmarks** (⭐/📌/🔖): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation. Native agent dots cover the agent part; manual bookmarks have no analog.
150	
151	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.
152	
153	## See also
154	
155	- [tmux setup](tmux/README.md) · [Television (tv)](tv.md) · [sesh](sesh.md) · [workmux](workmux.md)
156	- [Tool managers — where tools come from](../this_repo/tool-managers.md)
157
```

```text
1	# 24_herdr.sh - herdr workspace layout helpers (shared backend; bash 4+ / zsh).
2	# https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr
3	#
4	# herdr-native analogs of the sesh/tmux helpers in 22_sesh.sh. herdr's model is
5	# Workspace -> Tab -> Pane (tmux is Session -> Window -> Pane), and its CLI
6	# (`herdr workspace|tab|pane|agent …`) is the scripting surface that replaces
7	# `tmux new-session/split-window`.
8	#
9	# Backend that powers the user-facing commands and their aliases:
10	#   herdr-vibe / hvibe  — parametric multi-agent pack in a new workspace
11	#                         (N agent panes + lazygit tab + nvim tab)
12	#   herdr-code / hcode  — repo-scoped single-agent layout
13	#                         (nvim | agent split + btop monitor tab)
14	#
15	# REUSE: the *pure* (multiplexer-agnostic) helpers from 22_sesh.sh are reused
16	# verbatim — `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent` (specstory
17	# wrapping), `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` (shell|kill|restart post-exit behavior).
18	# 22_sesh.sh sorts before this file, so they are defined by the time hvibe/hcode
19	# run. Only the tmux calls are swapped for `herdr …` CLI calls.
20	#
21	# Bash baseline: 4+ (same array-slicing idiom as svibe; no `local -A`).
22	
23	# Skip entirely if herdr isn't installed (it's a trial tool, not on every host).
24	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
25	
26	# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
27	
28	# Echo the workspace_id of an existing workspace whose label == $1 (else empty).
29	# Used for idempotency: re-running hvibe/hcode in a repo focuses the existing
30	# workspace instead of stacking duplicates (mirrors svibe's has-session check).
31	function _herdr_ws_by_label() {
32	    herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null \
33	        | jq -r --arg l "$1" '.result.workspaces[]? | select(.label==$l) | .workspace_id' 2>/dev/null \
34	        | head -1
35	}
36	
37	# Compose the shell command for one agent pane: specstory-wrap then on-exit-wrap.
38	# $1=agent  $2=specstory_mode(auto|never)  $3=on_exit(shell|kill|restart)
39	function _herdr_agent_cmd() {
40	    local inner
41	    inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$2")
42	    _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$3" "${1:-agent}"
43	}
44	
45	# Create a labeled tab in workspace $1 (cwd $2, label $3) and run command $4 in
46	# its root pane. `tab create` returns the new pane id at .result.root_pane.
47	# $1=workspace_id  $2=cwd  $3=label  $4=command
48	function _herdr_tool_tab() {
49	    local pane
50	    pane=$(herdr tab create --workspace "$1" --cwd "$2" --label "$3" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
51	        | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
52	    [ -n "$pane" ] && herdr pane run "$pane" "$4" >/dev/null 2>&1
53	}
54	
55	# ── hvibe: parametric multi-agent pack ──────────────────────────────────────
56	#
57	# A herdr "vibe" workspace: tab "agents" with N agent panes (side-by-side
58	# splits by default), tab "git" (lazygit), tab "edit" (nvim). Built directly
59	# with herdr CLI calls so pane count stays parametric.
60	#
61	# Workspace label: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (idempotent — re-running focuses it).
62	# Refuses outside a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo).
63	#
64	# Each agent pane is specstory-wrapped (known providers) and on-exit-wrapped,
65	# exactly like `svibe` — the wrapping helpers are shared, only the layout calls
66	# differ. herdr auto-detects agent state per pane, so all N agents surface
67	# individually in the sidebar even when they share the "agents" tab.
68	#
69	# Two modes for choosing agents (same as svibe):
70	#   Homogeneous (positional):  hvibe 3 codex        → 3 panes all codex
71	#   Heterogeneous (--agents):  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode
72	#
73	# --tab-per-agent puts each agent in its OWN tab (own rolled-up state dot in the
74	# sidebar) instead of side-by-side splits — better for many agents, since herdr
75	# has no even-out-splits command.
76	#
77	# Usage:
78	#   hvibe                                       # auto N × claude (specstory)
79	#   hvibe 2                                     # 2× claude
80	#   hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× specstory run codex
81	#   hvibe 2 opencode                            # 2× opencode (raw)
82	#   hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
83	#   hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
84	#   hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude, no md auto-save
85	#   hvibe --on-exit restart 2 codex             # auto-respawn loop
86	#   hvibe -p ~/repo 2 claude                    # explicit path
87	#   hvibe --no-attach 2 claude                  # create in background
88	function herdr-vibe() {
89	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hvibe: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
90	
91	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
92	    local n_agents=0 n_agents_set=0 agent_cli="claude" agents_csv="" tab_per_agent=0
93	    local min_width="${HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
94	    # Stagger between pane launches so agents that share a global resource at
95	    # cold start (opencode's single SQLite DB + WAL pragma) don't race. Set 0
96	    # to launch all at once. Same rationale as svibe's SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER.
97	    local launch_stagger="${HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER:-0.25}"
98	
99	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
100	        case "$1" in
101	            -p|--path)       target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
102	            --on-exit)       on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
103	            --agents)        agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
104	            --min-width)     min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
105	            --tab-per-agent) tab_per_agent=1; shift ;;
106	            --no-specstory)  specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
107	            --specstory)     specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
108	            --no-attach)     no_attach=1; shift ;;
109	            -h|--help)
110	                cat <<'EOF'
111	hvibe — herdr multi-agent pack (herdr analog of svibe)
112	
113	Usage:
114	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
115	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
116	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
117	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]
118	
119	Builds a new herdr workspace `vibe/<repo>`:
120	  tab "agents" — N agent panes (side-by-side splits; each auto-detected in
121	                 the sidebar). --tab-per-agent → one tab per agent instead.
122	  tab "git"    — lazygit (falls back to `git status`)
123	  tab "edit"   — nvim
124	Idempotent: re-running in the same repo focuses the existing workspace.
125	Requires:  a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into one).
126	
127	Two modes for choosing agents:
128	  Homogeneous:    hvibe 3 codex → 3 panes all codex
129	  Heterogeneous:  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode  (list length = panes)
130	
131	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
132	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
133	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
134	
135	--on-exit MODE (per pane, on Ctrl+C / clean exit):
136	  shell (default) — drop to a shell with a re-run hint
137	  kill            — let the pane close
138	  restart         — auto-respawn in a loop
139	
140	--min-width COLS (default $HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80) auto-picks N when omitted:
141	  N = clamp(term_width / min-width, 1, 6)
142	$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER (seconds, default 0.25) delays each pane launch.
143	
144	Examples:
145	  hvibe                                       # auto N × claude
146	  hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× codex
147	  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
148	  hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
149	  hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude
150	EOF
151	                return 0 ;;
152	            -*)              echo "hvibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
153	            *)               break ;;
154	        esac
155	    done
156	
157	    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
158	        echo "hvibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
159	        return 1
160	    fi
161	    if ! [[ "$launch_stagger" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
162	        echo "hvibe: HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER must be a non-negative number (got: $launch_stagger)" >&2
163	        return 1
164	    fi
165	
166	    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"
167	
168	    # Build the agents array (same two paths as svibe; mixing is rejected).
169	    local -a agents
170	    agents=()
171	    if [ -n "$agents_csv" ]; then
172	        if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
173	            echo "hvibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
174	            return 1
175	        fi
176	        local tok
177	        while IFS= read -r tok; do
178	            tok="${tok## }"; tok="${tok%% }"
179	            [ -n "$tok" ] && agents+=( "$tok" )

181	        if [ "${#agents[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
182	            echo "hvibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
183	            return 1
184	        fi
185	    else
186	        if [ $# -gt 0 ] && [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
187	            n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
188	        fi
189	        [ $# -gt 0 ] && agent_cli="$1"
190	        # Auto-pick N from terminal width. Clamp [1,6] (lower than svibe's 12:
191	        # herdr right-splits nest, so many panes get cramped — use
192	        # --tab-per-agent for more).
193	        if [ "$n_agents_set" -eq 0 ]; then
194	            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
195	            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
196	            (( n_agents > 6 )) && n_agents=6
197	        fi
198	        local k
199	        for (( k = 0; k < n_agents; k++ )); do agents+=( "$agent_cli" ); done
200	    fi
201	
202	    case "$on_exit" in
203	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
204	        *) echo "hvibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
205	    esac
206	
207	    # Resolve git root (required, like svibe).
208	    local repo_root
209	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then

211	    else
212	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
213	    fi
214	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
215	        echo "hvibe: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo." >&2
216	        return 1
217	    fi
218	
219	    # Fail-fast: every agent CLI must exist in PATH.
220	    local a missing=""
221	    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
222	        command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing $a"
223	    done
224	    if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
225	        echo "hvibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH:$missing" >&2
226	        echo "       Available: claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini (install as needed)." >&2
227	        return 1
228	    fi
229	
230	    local repo label
231	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
232	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/$repo")
233	
234	    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
235	    local existing
236	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
237	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
238	        echo "hvibe: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
239	        [ "$no_attach" -eq 1 ] || herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
240	        return 0
241	    fi
242	
243	    # Create the workspace; capture the initial pane/tab (become the first agent).
244	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
245	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
246	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
247	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
248	    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
249	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
250	        echo "hvibe: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
251	        return 1
252	    fi
253	
254	    local first_agent="${agents[@]:0:1}"
255	    if [ "$tab_per_agent" -eq 1 ]; then
256	        # One tab per agent. Initial tab hosts the first agent (labeled by it).
257	        herdr tab rename "$t0" "$first_agent" >/dev/null 2>&1
258	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
259	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
260	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
261	            _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" "$a" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")"
262	        done
263	    else
264	        # Side-by-side splits in one "agents" tab. Thread `prev` so each new pane
265	        # splits off the previous one → predictable left-to-right columns.
266	        herdr tab rename "$t0" agents >/dev/null 2>&1
267	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
268	        # Even columns: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so set each
269	        # split's ratio explicitly. --ratio is the fraction KEPT by the pane
270	        # being split (the left one); the new pane gets the rest. Splitting the
271	        # rightmost pane on step m (of N-1) with ratio 1/(N-m+1) leaves every
272	        # finalized column at 1/N width.
273	        local n_total="${#agents[@]}" prev="$p0" np m=1 ratio

275	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
276	            ratio=$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.4f\", 1/($n_total-$m+1)}")
277	            np=$(herdr pane split "$prev" --direction right --ratio "$ratio" --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \

283	            m=$((m+1))

13	## Option A — keybinding in `create_config.toml`
14	
15	Bind e.g. `prefix+alt+v` → `hvibe`, `prefix+alt+c` → `hcode`:
16	
17	```toml
18	[[keys.command]]
19	key = "prefix+alt+v"
20	type = "pane"      # temporary pane, closes when the command exits
21	command = "hvibe -p \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD\""
22	```
23	
24	Design calls / caveats:
25	- `type="pane"` opens a **tiling split**, not a floating popup (herdr issue [#785](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/785) — centered float for `[[keys.command]]` is *not planned*; only plugins get `--placement overlay`). The launcher pane is short-lived (hvibe creates + focuses a new workspace, then the launcher pane closes), so the transient split is tolerable — verify it doesn't leave a stray pane behind.
26	- `hvibe` resolves the git root from `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`; if that pane isn't in a repo, hvibe errors (by design). Consider a `type="pane"` so the error is visible before the pane closes.

## 1. 有沒有 herdr 的 docs?

有,而且蠻完整:**[`docs/tools/herdr.md`](docs/tools/herdr.md)**(157 行,已在 mkdocs nav)。涵蓋 model vs tmux、keybindings、`hvibe`/`hcode`、herdr-plus plugin、persistence、agent-state、config writeback。

## 2. Session vs "spaces"(workspace)的層級

你的直覺對——確實多了一層。實際的樹是:

```
herdr server
 └─ Session      ← default / test …(多個具名 session,各自獨立 server + socket)
     └─ Workspace ← 你看到的 "spaces"(每個 repo 一個,hvibe 建的就是這層)
         └─ Tab   ← 相當於 tmux window
             └─ Pane
```

- **Session** 這層比較像「tmux 開多個 socket / 多個 server」,不是 tmux session。`herdr.sock` 是 default,具名的在 `sessions/<name>/herdr.socket`。
- 深度是 **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane**,比 tmux 的 Session → Window → Pane 多一層(Workspace)。docs 的「Model differences」有寫 Workspace→Tab→Pane,但**沒寫最上面 Session 可以有多個**——這是缺口。

## 3. `--remote` 怎麼用 + 你的錯誤

模型:`herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]` 會在本機跑一個 **thin client**,SSH 到目標、**自動幫你在遠端裝好對應平台的 herdr server binary**、起/接遠端 session,並把本機剪貼簿(含貼圖)橋接過去、沿用你本機的 keybindings。

你的 `Connection closed by 192.168.31.67 port 22` 是**暫時性的**,不是設定問題,證據:
- 我剛用 key(`~/.ssh/azure_vm1`)非互動 SSH 到 `local_ubuntu` **成功**(`Linux x86_64`)。
- 遠端目前**沒裝 herdr**(`NO_HERDR`),但 `--remote` 會自動裝,所以不是阻礙。
- 你的 `herdr-client.log` 顯示**昨天 (07-03) `--remote` 是正常運作的**(一直在 bridge 剪貼簿貼圖到 remote server)。

**→ 直接重跑 `herdr --remote local_ubuntu` 應該就會過**。若持續失敗,失敗當下看 `herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log`;可疑點是 sshd 對快速多連線的 `MaxStartups` 限制(herdr 的 `[remote].manage_ssh_config=true` 會補 keepalive)。

## 4. hvibe 的幾個問題——實測結果

- **「在 herdr 內,hvibe 要能知道當前 session」→ 其實已經會了。** herdr CLI 會吃 `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`(進到某個 session 的 pane 時就會被設成該 session 的 socket)。hvibe 只是呼叫 `herdr workspace create …`,自然繼承這個環境變數 → workspace 就落在**當前 session**。我實測把 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` 指到 `test` session 的 socket,`herdr workspace list` 就轉去查 test session 了。所以這點是隱性 already-works。

- **真正的 bug:從 herdr *外面* 跑 hvibe 不會 attach。** hvibe 結尾是 `herdr workspace focus $ws`,而 `focus` 只會移動「已 attach 的 client」的焦點。你在純 terminal(沒有 client attach 到該 session)跑,workspace 建好了但畫面沒東西,得再手動 `herdr` 才進得去。**修法**:偵測不在 herdr 內(`HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID` 沒設)時,除非 `--no-attach`,結尾 `exec herdr session attach <session>`(或裸 `herdr`)把 UI 帶起來並聚焦新 workspace。

- **`--session` 沒被當參數暴露。** hvibe/hcode 目前無 `--session NAME`;要指定別的 session 只能先自己 `export HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=…`。合理做法:加 `--session NAME`,把 NAME 解析成 socket(default=`herdr.sock`,具名=`sessions/<name>/herdr.socket`),在 herdr 內時預設用 ambient session,在外面時就 attach 到它。

這些在 [`backlog/hvibe-herdr-surfacing.md`](backlog/hvibe-herdr-surfacing.md) 有部分相關(那份講的是「從 herdr UI 內綁鍵叫起 hvibe」,跟你這次的 attach/session 是不同軸),可以合併補上。

---

99	#   auto  — wrap if known provider, raw otherwise (the historical default)
100	#   never — pass through raw regardless (CLI flag --no-specstory sets this)
101	function _sesh_wrap_agent() {
102	    local agent="$1" specstory_mode="${2:-auto}"
103	    if [ "$specstory_mode" = "never" ]; then
104	        # Even an empty agent goes raw → caller's responsibility to pick a

126	# Build a wrapper command that controls what happens when the inner command
127	# exits (Ctrl+C, agent quit, crash). `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`:
128	#   shell   — print a hint, then drop into $SHELL so user can restart agent,
129	#             switch to lazygit, kill the pane manually, etc. (default)
130	#   kill    — let the pane close on exit (tmux default `remain-on-exit off`)
131	#   restart — wrap in `while true; do CMD; sleep 1; done` so the agent
132	#             auto-respawns. Use Ctrl+C twice quickly to break the loop and
133	#             land in shell.
134	#
135	# Args: $1=inner_cmd, $2=mode, $3=label_for_hint
136	# Stdout: the wrapped shell command (single string suitable for `tmux
137	# new-window … "<cmd>"`). Quoting is structured so user $SHELL is the one
138	# evaluating the inner command — we don't double-eval.
139	function _sesh_on_exit_wrap() {
140	    local inner="$1" mode="$2" label="${3:-agent}"
141	    # Ctrl+C sends SIGINT to the entire foreground process group, so the
142	    # wrapper shell itself dies before it can print the hint or exec the
143	    # login shell — the pane just vanishes. `trap '' INT` makes the wrapper
144	    # ignore SIGINT; the inner command still receives it and exits normally,
145	    # then control returns to the wrapper which prints the hint as intended.
146	    # (Tools that install their own SIGINT handler — btop, htop, less — were

149	    local guard="trap '' INT;"
150	    case "$mode" in

164	}

166	# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).
167	# Lightweight: drops you into a plain shell at $PWD with NO startup command.
168	# For an editor-first session use `scode` (repo-aware, full layout) or just
169	# launch nvim manually inside the new session.

171	# Smart argument handling:
172	#   shere                              # plain shell at $PWD, no command
173	#   shere specstory run codex          # bare args → treated as command
174	#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
175	#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path, plain shell
176	#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
177	function sesh-here() {
178	    local cmd="" target=""
179	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
180	        case "$1" in
181	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
182	            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
183	            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
184	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
185	        esac
186	    done
187	    [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$cmd" ] && cmd="$*"
188	    target="${target:-$PWD}"
189	    if [ -n "$cmd" ]; then
190	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$target"
191	    else
192	        # Bypass sesh's default_session.startup_command (nvim) for a plain
193	        # shell. We create the session via tmux directly, then attach. This
194	        # also means the wildcard startup_command (project layout) is
195	        # bypassed — `shere` is intentionally lightweight; use `scode`,
196	        # `svibe`, or `sesh connect <path>` for layouts.
197	        local session
198	        session=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
199	        _sesh_ensure_session "$session" "$target"
200	        _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
201	    fi
202	}

206	#   sroot                              # default startup_command
207	#   sroot specstory run codex          # bare args → command
208	#   sroot -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
209	function sesh-root() {
210	    local cmd="" root
211	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
212	        case "$1" in
213	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
214	            -*)           shift ;;

216	        esac
217	    done
218	    [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$cmd" ] && cmd="$*"
219	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
220	    if [ -n "$cmd" ]; then
221	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$root"
222	    else
223	        sesh connect "$root"
224	    fi
225	}
226	
227	alias shere='sesh-here'
228	alias sroot='sesh-root'
229	alias scode='sesh-code'
230	alias svibe='sesh-vibe'
231	
232	# ── scode: repo-aware coding-agent layout ───────────────────────────────────
233	#
234	# Open the coding-agent layout (nvim 75% | specstory-wrapped agent 25%, btop
235	# window) in a session NAMED FOR THE CURRENT REPO, so different repos don't
236	# collide on the single `coding-agent` session name.
237	#
238	# Session naming:
239	#   In repo /Volumes/Data/Program/Personal/foo  → session `coding-agent/foo`
240	#   Same repo re-invocation                     → attach (no duplicate)
241	#   Different repo                              → new session `coding-agent/<other>`
242	#
243	# Outside a git repo the function refuses with a hint to use `shere` or `svibe`
244	# (the heavy layout doesn't make sense for ad-hoc directories).
245	#
246	# Agent wrapping: known specstory providers (claude/codex/cursor/droid/gemini)
247	# are auto-wrapped in `specstory run X` for markdown auto-save. Others
248	# (opencode today) pass through raw — see _sesh_wrap_agent + backlog entry
249	# `specstory-opencode-support` for the upstream tracking.
250	#
251	# Exit behavior: `--on-exit shell` (default) drops to a shell with a hint when
252	# the agent exits, so Ctrl+C doesn't kill the pane. Use `--on-exit kill` for
253	# the old behavior, or `--on-exit restart` for an auto-respawn loop.
254	#
255	# Usage:
256	#   scode                              # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
257	#   scode codex                        # specstory run codex
258	#   scode opencode                     # opencode raw (not yet a specstory provider)
259	#   scode --on-exit kill claude        # Ctrl+C kills the right pane
260	#   scode --on-exit restart codex      # codex auto-respawns on crash
261	#   scode -p ~/some/other/repo         # explicit repo path
262	#   scode --no-attach                  # create session in background, don't switch
263	function sesh-code() {
264	    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
265	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
266	        case "$1" in
267	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
268	            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
269	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
270	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
271	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
272	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
273	            --agents)
274	                echo "scode: --agents is svibe-only (scode is single-agent)." >&2
275	                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: svibe --agents '$2'" >&2
276	                return 1 ;;
277	            -h|--help)
278	                cat <<'EOF'
279	scode — open repo-scoped coding-agent layout
280	
281	Usage: scode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
282	             [--no-attach] [AGENT]
283	
284	Layout: window `editor` (nvim 75% | agent 25%) + window `monitor` (btop).
285	Session name: `coding-agent/<repo-basename>` (one session per repo).
286	Requires:     git repo (errors otherwise — use `shere` or `svibe`).
287	
288	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
289	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
290	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
291	
292	--on-exit MODE controls what happens when ANY pane command exits/Ctrl+C
293	(applies to the agent pane, the nvim pane, and the btop monitor window):
294	  shell    (default) — drop to shell with a hint, command re-runnable
295	  kill                — let the pane/window close (tmux default)
296	  restart             — auto-respawn the command in a loop
297	
298	Examples:
299	  scode                            # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
300	  scode codex                      # right pane: specstory run codex
301	  scode opencode                   # right pane: opencode (raw)
302	  scode --no-specstory claude      # right pane: claude (raw, no markdown auto-save)
303	  scode --on-exit kill claude      # right pane closes when claude exits
304	  scode -p ~/work/foo              # explicit repo path
305	EOF
306	                return 0 ;;
307	            -*)             echo "scode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
308	            *)              [ -z "$agent" ] && agent="$1"; shift ;;
309	        esac
310	    done
311	
312	    case "$on_exit" in
313	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
314	        *) echo "scode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
315	    esac
316	
317	    # Resolve repo root
318	    local repo_root
319	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
320	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
321	    else
322	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
323	    fi
324	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
325	        echo "scode: not inside a git repo." >&2
326	        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell, or \`svibe\` for a vibe layout in any dir." >&2
327	        return 1
328	    fi
329	
330	    # Validate agent CLI exists in PATH (fail-fast). Specstory itself isn't
331	    # checked here — if the user passed a known provider but specstory is
332	    # missing, the pane will exit with specstory's error message and
333	    # --on-exit=shell will leave a shell to read it.
334	    if [ -n "$agent" ] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
335	        echo "scode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
336	        return 1
337	    fi
338	
339	    local repo_name session
340	    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
341	    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/${repo_name}")
342	
343	    # If session already exists, just attach (idempotent — solves the
344	    # cross-repo collision problem the old single `coding-agent` session had).
345	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
346	        [ "$no_attach" -eq 1 ] || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
347	        return 0
348	    fi
349	
350	    # Create session + build layout directly with tmux commands (see svibe
351	    # comment block for why not tmuxp).
352	    #
353	    # Window 1 "editor": nvim (left, will be 75%) | wrapped agent (right, 25%)
354	    # Window 2 "monitor": btop (or htop / top fallback)
355	    local agent_inner agent_cmd
356	    agent_inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$agent" "$specstory_mode")
357	    agent_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$agent_inner" "$on_exit" "${agent:-agent}")
358	
359	    # nvim and monitor get the same on-exit treatment as the agent so that
360	    # quitting them drops to a shell with a re-launch hint instead of the
361	    # pane/window vanishing.
362	    local nvim_cmd monitor_inner monitor_cmd
363	    nvim_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")
364	
365	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n editor "$nvim_cmd"
366	    tmux split-window -h -t "${session}:editor" -c "$repo_root" "$agent_cmd"
367	    # main-vertical layout, then size the LEFT pane to 75% of window width
368	    tmux select-layout -t "${session}:editor" main-vertical >/dev/null
369	    tmux resize-pane -t "${session}:editor.1" -x 75% 2>/dev/null
370	
371	    # Monitor window
372	    if   command -v btop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=btop
373	    elif command -v htop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=htop
374	    else                                       monitor_inner=top
375	    fi
376	    monitor_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$monitor_inner" "$on_exit" "$monitor_inner")
377	    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n monitor -c "$repo_root" "$monitor_cmd"
378	
379	    # Focus editor window, left (nvim) pane
380	    tmux select-window -t "${session}:editor"
381	    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:editor.1"
382	
383	    [ "$no_attach" -eq 1 ] || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
384	}
385	
386	# ── svibe: parametric multi-agent vibe layout ───────────────────────────────
387	#
388	# A "vibe coding" session: window 1 has N agent panes (default 4), window 2
389	# is lazygit, window 3 is nvim. Built directly with tmux split/new-window
390	# commands so it stays parametric (tmuxp YAML can't express dynamic pane counts).
391	#
392	# Session naming: `vibe/<dir-basename>` — collision-safe across directories.
393	# Refuses outside a git repo (use `shere` for plain shells in arbitrary dirs).
394	#
395	# Each agent pane is wrapped in `specstory run X` (for known providers, opt
396	# out with --no-specstory) and additionally wrapped in an exit handler
397	# controlled by `--on-exit MODE` — same semantics as `scode`. Default `shell`
398	# keeps the pane open with a hint after the agent exits, so Ctrl+C is
399	# recoverable.
400	#
401	# Two modes for choosing which agents run:
402	#   1. Homogeneous (positional): `svibe 4 codex` → 4 panes all running codex
403	#   2. Heterogeneous (--agents):  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`
404	#                                 → 4 panes running those specific agents
405	#                                 (list LENGTH determines pane count;
406	#                                 positional N_AGENTS is rejected to avoid
407	#                                 ambiguity)
408	#
409	# Usage:
410	#   svibe                                          # 4× claude (specstory)
411	#   svibe 2                                        # 2× claude
412	#   svibe 4 codex                                  # 4× specstory run codex
413	#   svibe 3 opencode                               # 3× opencode (raw)
414	#   svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode     # 4 panes, mixed
415	#   svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill  # 2 panes, mixed, hard exit
416	#   svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                  # 4× claude (raw, no md auto-save)
417	#   svibe --on-exit restart 4 codex                # auto-respawn loop
418	#   svibe -p ~/repo 4 claude                       # explicit path
419	#   svibe --no-attach 4 claude                     # create in background
420	function sesh-vibe() {
421	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
422	    local n_agents=4 n_agents_set=0
423	    local agent_cli="claude"
424	    local agents_csv=""
425	    local min_width="${SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
426	    # Seconds to wait between launching each agent pane. Default 0.25s staggers
427	    # startup so DB-backed agents (opencode opens a single global SQLite DB and
428	    # runs `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`, which needs a brief exclusive lock)
429	    # don't race on a simultaneous cold start. Set 0 to launch all at once.
430	    # See pitfalls/opencode-concurrent-launch-wal-pragma-fails.md.
431	    local launch_stagger="${SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER:-0.25}"
432	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
433	        case "$1" in
434	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
435	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
436	            --agents)       agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
437	            --min-width)    min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
438	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
439	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
440	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
441	            -h|--help)
442	                cat <<'EOF'
443	svibe — parametric multi-agent vibe layout
444	
445	Usage:
446	  svibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
447	        [--min-width COLS] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
448	  svibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
449	        [--min-width COLS] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]
450	
451	Default: svibe           (N auto-picked from term_width ÷ min-width, clamp [1,12])
452	  window 1 "agents" — N agent panes (columns if all fit at ≥min-width, else tiled)
453	  window 2 "git"    — lazygit
454	  window 3 "edit"   — nvim
455	
456	Two modes for choosing agents:
457	  Homogeneous:    `svibe 4 codex` → 4 panes all codex
458	  Heterogeneous:  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`
459	                  → 4 panes (one each, in order); list length = pane count
460	
461	Session name: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (collision-safe per directory).
462	Requires:     git repo (use `shere` for plain shells elsewhere).
463	
464	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
465	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
466	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
467	
468	--on-exit MODE controls per-pane behavior on Ctrl+C / clean exit
469	(applies to all agent panes, the lazygit window, and the nvim window):
470	  shell    (default) — drop to shell with a hint, command re-runnable
471	  kill                — let the pane/window close (tmux default)
472	  restart             — auto-respawn the command in a loop
473	
474	--min-width COLS sets the minimum readable per-pane width (default: value of
475	$SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80). It drives two decisions:
476	  • auto-pick N when you don't pass a count (N = term_width / min-width)
477	  • columns vs tiled in the agents window: columns when all N panes fit at
478	    ≥COLS wide side-by-side, otherwise tiled grid
479	Example on a 240-col terminal:
480	  min-width 80   → auto N=3, three even-horizontal columns
481	  min-width 120  → auto N=2, two even-horizontal columns
482	
483	$SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER (seconds, default 0.25) delays each pane launch so
484	agents that share a global resource at cold start (e.g. opencode's single
485	SQLite DB + WAL pragma) don't race. Set 0 to launch all panes at once.
486	
487	Examples:
488	  svibe                                            # auto N × claude, width-aware layout
489	  svibe 2                                          # 2× claude
490	  svibe 4 codex                                    # 4× codex
491	  svibe 6 opencode                                 # 6× opencode (heavy)
492	  svibe --min-width 120                            # wider panes → fewer auto columns
493	  svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode       # 4 panes, mixed
494	  svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill    # 2 panes, mixed
495	  svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                    # raw claude, no auto-save
496	EOF
497	                return 0 ;;
498	            -*)             echo "svibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
499	            *)              break ;;
500	        esac
501	    done
502	
503	    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
504	        echo "svibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
505	        return 1
506	    fi
507	
508	    # Accept an integer or decimal number of seconds (e.g. 0, 0.25, 1). Used as
509	    # a `sleep` argument between pane launches.
510	    if ! [[ "$launch_stagger" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
511	        echo "svibe: SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER must be a non-negative number of seconds (got: $launch_stagger)" >&2
512	        return 1
513	    fi
514	
515	    # Current terminal width, used for auto-picking N (when the user didn't
516	    # pass a count) and for the columns-vs-tiled cutover. $COLUMNS is
517	    # auto-maintained by both shells on SIGWINCH; tput is a fallback for
518	    # non-interactive invocation; 200 is a generous last resort.
519	    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"
520	
521	    # Build the agents array. Two paths:
522	    #   --agents claude,codex,…  → split csv, list length = pane count
523	    #   positional [N] [CLI]     → repeat CLI N times (N auto-picked if omitted)
524	    # Mixing both is rejected to keep semantics unambiguous.
525	    local -a agents
526	    agents=()
527	    if [ -n "$agents_csv" ]; then
528	        if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
529	            echo "svibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
530	            echo "       Pick one. (e.g. drop the trailing args)" >&2
531	            return 1
532	        fi
533	        # POSIX-portable CSV parse: tr commas → newlines, while-read each.
534	        # Avoids zsh's `${=var}` word-splitting flag (which bash lacks) and
535	        # zsh's `read -A` vs bash's `read -a` flag-case mismatch.
536	        local tok
537	        while IFS= read -r tok; do
538	            # Trim single leading/trailing space (matches original behavior).
539	            tok="${tok## }"
540	            tok="${tok%% }"
541	            [ -n "$tok" ] && agents+=( "$tok" )
542	        done < <(printf '%s\n' "$agents_csv" | tr ',' '\n')
543	        if [ "${#agents[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
544	            echo "svibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
545	            return 1
546	        fi
547	    else
548	        # Positional: [n_agents] [agent_cli]
549	        if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
550	            if [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
551	                n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
552	            fi
553	        fi
554	        [ $# -gt 0 ] && agent_cli="$1"
555	
556	        # Auto-pick N from terminal width when the user didn't pass one.
557	        # N = clamp(term_width / min_width, 1, 12). On a 240-col terminal
558	        # with min-width 80 that's N=3; at min-width 120, N=2.
559	        if [ "$n_agents_set" -eq 0 ]; then
560	            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
561	            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
562	            (( n_agents > 12 )) && n_agents=12
563	        fi
564	
565	        # Build a homogeneous array of length n_agents
566	        local k
567	        for (( k = 0; k < n_agents; k++ )); do
568	            agents+=( "$agent_cli" )
569	        done
570	    fi
571	
572	    case "$on_exit" in
573	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
574	        *) echo "svibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
575	    esac
576	
577	    if (( ${#agents[@]} < 1 || ${#agents[@]} > 12 )); then
578	        echo "svibe: agent count = ${#agents[@]} out of range [1, 12]" >&2
579	        return 1
580	    fi
581	
582	    # Resolve repo root
583	    local repo_root
584	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
585	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
586	    else
587	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
588	    fi
589	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
590	        echo "svibe: not inside a git repo." >&2
591	        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell in arbitrary directories." >&2
592	        return 1
593	    fi
594	
595	    # Validate ALL agent CLIs exist in PATH (fail-fast — we don't want to
596	    # build a 4-pane layout where one pane is dead). De-dup the list to keep
597	    # the error message readable. Requires bash 4+ for `local -A`.
598	    local -a missing
599	    missing=()
600	    local -A seen
601	    local a
602	    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
603	        [ -n "${seen[$a]:-}" ] && continue
604	        seen[$a]=1
605	        if ! command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
606	            missing+=( "$a" )
607	        fi
608	    done
609	    if [ "${#missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
610	        echo "svibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH: ${missing[*]}" >&2
611	        local _avail=""
612	        for c in claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini; do
613	            command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && _avail="$_avail$c "
614	        done
615	        echo "       Available: $_avail" >&2
616	        return 1
617	    fi
618	
619	    local repo_name session
620	    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
621	    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/${repo_name}")
622	
623	    # Idempotent: existing session = just attach
624	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
625	        [ "$no_attach" -eq 1 ] || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
626	        return 0
627	    fi
628	
629	    # Build wrapped command for each agent (the wrapping is pane-specific so
630	    # we can mix providers in one window).
631	    #
632	    # Helper: turn agent name → fully-wrapped tmux command string.
633	    _vibe_agent_cmd() {
634	        local inner
635	        inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$specstory_mode")
636	        _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$on_exit" "$1"
637	    }
638	
639	    # ── Build the session ───────────────────────────────────────────────
640	    # Window 1: agents — start with first pane running the first agent.
641	    # `${agents[@]:0:1}` is bash-style array slicing (0-indexed); zsh
642	    # supports the same syntax on `[@]`, sidestepping the bash-0/zsh-1
643	    # indexing fork.
644	    local first_agent="${agents[@]:0:1}"
645	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n agents \
646	        "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "$first_agent")"
647	
648	    # Pick window layout based on agent count vs what fits as readable
649	    # side-by-side columns at --min-width:
650	    #   N ≤ term_width / min_width → even-horizontal (columns)
651	    #   otherwise                  → tiled (grid — columns would be too narrow)
652	    local max_columns=$(( term_width / min_width ))
653	    (( max_columns < 1 )) && max_columns=1
654	    local svibe_layout
655	    if (( ${#agents[@]} <= max_columns )); then
656	        svibe_layout="even-horizontal"
657	    else
658	        svibe_layout="tiled"
659	    fi
660	
661	    # Add remaining panes (skip the first via array slice).
662	    for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
663	        # Stagger launches so simultaneously-spawned agents don't race on a
664	        # shared resource at cold start (opencode's global SQLite DB + WAL
665	        # pragma — see pitfalls/opencode-concurrent-launch-wal-pragma-fails.md).
666	        [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
667	        tmux split-window -t "${session}:agents" -c "$repo_root" \
668	            "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "$a")"
669	        # Re-balance after each split so layout stays uniform
670	        tmux select-layout -t "${session}:agents" "$svibe_layout" >/dev/null
671	    done
672	
673	    unset -f _vibe_agent_cmd
674	
675	    # Window 2: git (lazygit if present)
676	    # lazygit and nvim get the same on-exit handling as agents — quitting
677	    # them drops to shell with a re-launch hint rather than killing the window.
678	    local git_cmd edit_cmd
679	    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
680	        git_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "lazygit" "$on_exit" "lazygit")
681	        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "$git_cmd"
682	    else
683	        # `git status; exec $SHELL` already lands in shell — no wrap needed.
684	        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "git status; exec \$SHELL"
685	    fi
686	
687	    # Window 3: edit (nvim)
688	    edit_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")
689	    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n edit -c "$repo_root" "$edit_cmd"
690	
691	    # Focus agents window, first pane
692	    tmux select-window -t "${session}:agents"
693	    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:agents.1"
694	
695	    [ "$no_attach" -eq 1 ] || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
696	}

The core issue is that if the target session server isn't running, we hit a chicken-and-egg problem: `herdr --session NAME` starts both server and client interactively, but that attaches before we can create the workspace. 1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2	
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4	
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6	
7	- **Install**:
8	  - macOS — Homebrew (`herdr` is in homebrew-core; managed by the `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
9	  - Linux — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr` (managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in the same role). No tarball, so no unarchive step.
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: brew on macOS; `herdr update` for the self-managed Linux binary
12	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **seed-once** (`dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml`, the `create_` prefix). herdr writes UI settings back into this file (see [Config writeback](#config-writeback-why-create_)), so chezmoi plants it on a fresh machine and then never touches it.
13	
14	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.
15
```

## 1. How svibe/scode decide whether to attach, and the exact attach vs switch-client commands

Both delegate the decision to the shared helper `_sesh_attach_or_switch`, which branches on `$TMUX`. The helper (lines 69-76):

```
69	function _sesh_attach_or_switch() {

73	    else

So:
- (a) already inside tmux → `tmux switch-client -t "$session"` (line 72)
- (b) plain terminal outside tmux → `tmux attach-session -t "$session"` (line 74)

Each command calls this helper in two places — the "session already exists" fast path and the end-of-build path — both gated on `--no-attach`:

## 2. exec vs child process

No `exec`. `_sesh_attach_or_switch` runs `tmux switch-client`/`tmux attach-session` as an ordinary child process (lines 72/74) — the calling shell is not replaced. (`exec` appears elsewhere in the file, but unrelated to attach: `exec </dev/tty` / `exec <&1` inside `sesh-sessions` at lines 29-30, and `exec \$SHELL -l` embedded inside the on-exit wrapper strings at lines 156/161 — those run inside the tmux panes, not in the launching shell.)

## 3. "Inside tmux" detection

Via the `$TMUX` environment variable, tested with `[ -n "$TMUX" ]` at line 71 (inside `_sesh_attach_or_switch`). That is the only place the inside/outside decision is made; svibe/scode themselves never test `$TMUX`.

## 4. `--no-attach` behavior

The flag sets a local `no_attach=1`:
- scode: line 272 `--no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;`
- svibe: line 440 `--no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;`

Every attach call site is guarded by `[ "$no_attach" -eq 1 ] || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"` (scode lines 346, 383; svibe lines 625, 695). When set, the session is created and laid out in the background (detached) and neither `switch-client` nor `attach-session` runs. The default is `no_attach=0` (scode line 264, svibe line 421).

`_sesh_git_root` (lines 57-59):

57	function _sesh_git_root() {
58	    git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null
59	}
```
No args. Echoes the absolute git repo root on stdout; stderr suppressed. Returns git's exit status (non-zero, empty stdout) when not in a repo. Callers capture it and test for empty (`repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)` then `[ -z "$repo_root" ]`).

`_sesh_sanitize` (lines 63-65):
```
63	function _sesh_sanitize() {
64	    printf '%s\n' "${1//[.:[:space:]]/-}"
65	}
```
Arg: `$1` = raw string. Echoes the string with every `.`, `:`, and whitespace char replaced by `-` (tmux forbids `.`/`:` in session names). Pure; no exit-status contract.

`_sesh_wrap_agent` (lines 101-124):
```
101	function _sesh_wrap_agent() {
102	    local agent="$1" specstory_mode="${2:-auto}"
103	    if [ "$specstory_mode" = "never" ]; then

Args: `$1`=agent, `$2`=specstory_mode (`auto`|`never`, default `auto`). Echoes the inner command string:
- `never` → `${agent:-claude}` (raw; empty agent falls back to `claude`)
- `auto` + empty/`specstory` → `specstory run`
- `auto` + `claude`/`codex`/`cursor`/`droid`/`gemini` → `specstory run <agent>`
- `auto` + anything else (e.g. `opencode`) → `<agent>` raw passthrough

139	function _sesh_on_exit_wrap() {

Args: `$1`=inner_cmd, `$2`=mode (`shell`|`kill`|`restart`), `$3`=label (default `agent`). Echoes a single shell-command string suitable for `tmux new-window …/split-window … "<cmd>"`:

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```md
# herdr: fix hvibe/hcode attach + add `--session`, document sessions & `--remote`

## Context

While using herdr the user hit a cluster of small gaps:

1. **`hvibe`/`hcode` don't attach when run from *outside* herdr.** They end with `herdr workspace focus`, which only moves an *already-attached* client's focus. From a plain terminal the workspace is created but nothing appears — you must then type `herdr` to attach. (Inside herdr, `workspace focus` already switches the live client, so that path is fine.)
2. **No way to target a specific herdr session.** A herdr server hosts multiple named **sessions** (`default`, `test`, …), each with its own socket. `hvibe`/`hcode` always hit whatever socket the CLI defaults to. There's no `--session` flag.
3. **Docs gaps.** `docs/tools/herdr.md` is thorough on Workspace→Tab→Pane but never documents (a) that a server hosts **multiple named sessions** (the extra top tree level the user discovered), nor (b) **`herdr --remote`** at all. No `herdr.zh-TW.md` exists.

Empirically verified during planning (we are currently running *inside* herdr's `default` session):
- `herdr` CLI subcommands honor the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — setting it to another session's `socket_path` routes `workspace create/list` to that session (probe workspace landed in `test`, invisible to `default`). There is **no** `--session`/`--socket` flag on the subcommands; the env var is the only lever.
- Ambient env inside a herdr pane: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (= current session's socket). So "am I inside herdr" = `[ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ]`, and inside herdr the CLI already targets the current session for free.
- `herdr session list --json` → `.sessions[] | {name, running, socket_path, default}` — authoritative name→socket resolver (the text table's `herdr.socket` is wrong; JSON says `herdr.sock`).
- `herdr --remote <target>` **auto-installs** a matching server binary on the remote over SSH; the user's `Connection closed by … port 22` was transient (key-auth SSH to `local_ubuntu` works now; the client log shows `--remote` bridging clipboard fine the day before).

Outcome: `hvibe`/`hcode` behave correctly from any context and accept `--session`; docs cover named sessions + remote; a zh-TW page and the missing zh-TW alias rows are added.

## Design decisions (resolved)

- **Attach from outside** mirrors `svibe`'s `_sesh_attach_or_switch` ($TMUX branch) but adapted: the repo-named object in herdr is the *workspace*, so we attach the whole **session** and rely on the prior `workspace focus` for landing spot. Attach runs as a **child process (no `exec`)**, exactly like svibe.
- **`--session` targeting** uses `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=…` (function-scoped export, auto-restored on return — supported in bash 4+ and zsh, matching the file's existing `local -a`/`[[ ]]`/process-subst baseline). Never a bare `export` (would leak the override into the user's shell).
- **`--session` when the target isn't running → error with a hint** (`herdr --session NAME` to start it first), rather than trying to spawn a headless server (chicken/egg with workspace creation). Small, predictable.
- Default session name is `default`; attach via bare `herdr` for default, `herdr session attach <name>` for named.

## Changes

### 1. `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` (primary)

Add two small shared helpers near the existing `_herdr_*` helpers:

\```sh
# Resolve the target session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session value.
# Echoes "<name>\t<socket_override_or_empty>". socket is non-empty ONLY when the
# caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit --session). Errors (return 1)
# if an explicit --session isn't a running session.
function _herdr_session_target() { … herdr session list --json | jq … ; }

# From OUTSIDE herdr, bring up a client so the just-focused workspace is visible.
# Inside herdr (HERDR_ENV set) the focus calls already switched the live client.
function _herdr_attach_if_outside() {
    [ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ] && return 0
    local session="${1:-default}"
    if [ "$session" = default ]; then herdr; else herdr session attach "$session"; fi
}
\```

In **both** `herdr-vibe` and `herdr-code`:
- Parse a new `--session NAME` flag (add to the `while`/`case`, the `-h` help text, and reject empty).
- After arg parsing, resolve the session:
  \```sh
  local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
  sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
  sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}; sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
  [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
  \```
  (When inside herdr with no `--session`, `sess_sock` is empty → ambient socket is used untouched; `sess_name` is derived for the — unused — attach path.)
- **Idempotent fast path** (`existing` found): keep `herdr workspace focus "$existing"` but append `_herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"` (still gated on `--no-attach`).
- **End-of-build attach block** (`if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then …`): keep the existing `workspace focus`/`tab focus`/`pane focus` lines, add `_herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"` as the last line inside the block.
- Update each `-h` help block: document `--session NAME` and the new "attaches when run outside herdr" behavior.

No change to the reused `_sesh_*` helpers or the layout logic.

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# herdr: fix hvibe/hcode attach + add `--session`, document sessions & `--remote`

## Context

While using herdr the user hit a cluster of small gaps:

1. **`hvibe`/`hcode` don't attach when run from *outside* herdr.** They end with `herdr workspace focus`, which only moves an *already-attached* client's focus. From a plain terminal the workspace is created but nothing appears — you must then type `herdr` to attach. (Inside herdr, `workspace focus` already switches the live client, so that path is fine.)
2. **No way to target a specific herdr session.** A herdr server hosts multiple named **sessions** (`default`, `test`, …), each with its own socket. `hvibe`/`hcode` always hit whatever socket the CLI defaults to. There's no `--session` flag.
3. **Docs gaps.** `docs/tools/herdr.md` is thorough on Workspace→Tab→Pane but never documents (a) that a server hosts **multiple named sessions** (the extra top tree level the user discovered), nor (b) **`herdr --remote`** at all. No `herdr.zh-TW.md` exists.

Empirically verified during planning (we are currently running *inside* herdr's `default` session):
- `herdr` CLI subcommands honor the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — setting it to another session's `socket_path` routes `workspace create/list` to that session (probe workspace landed in `test`, invisible to `default`). There is **no** `--session`/`--socket` flag on the subcommands; the env var is the only lever.
- Ambient env inside a herdr pane: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (= current session's socket). So "am I inside herdr" = `[ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ]`, and inside herdr the CLI already targets the current session for free.
- `herdr session list --json` → `.sessions[] | {name, running, socket_path, default}` — authoritative name→socket resolver (the text table's `herdr.socket` is wrong; JSON says `herdr.sock`).
- `herdr --remote <target>` **auto-installs** a matching server binary on the remote over SSH; the user's `Connection closed by … port 22` was transient (key-auth SSH to `local_ubuntu` works now; the client log shows `--remote` bridging clipboard fine the day before).

Outcome: `hvibe`/`hcode` behave correctly from any context and accept `--session`; docs cover named sessions + remote; a zh-TW page and the missing zh-TW alias rows are added.

## Design decisions (resolved)

- **Attach from outside** mirrors `svibe`'s `_sesh_attach_or_switch` ($TMUX branch) but adapted: the repo-named object in herdr is the *workspace*, so we attach the whole **session** and rely on the prior `workspace focus` for landing spot. Attach runs as a **child process (no `exec`)**, exactly like svibe.
- **`--session` targeting** uses `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=…` (function-scoped export, auto-restored on return — supported in bash 4+ and zsh, matching the file's existing `local -a`/`[[ ]]`/process-subst baseline). Never a bare `export` (would leak the override into the user's shell).
- **`--session` when the target isn't running → error with a hint** (`herdr --session NAME` to start it first), rather than trying to spawn a headless server (chicken/egg with workspace creation). Small, predictable.
- Default session name is `default`; attach via bare `herdr` for default, `herdr session attach <name>` for named.

## Changes

### 1. `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` (primary)

Add two small shared helpers near the existing `_herdr_*` helpers:

```sh
# Resolve the target session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session value.
# Echoes "<name>\t<socket_override_or_empty>". socket is non-empty ONLY when the
# caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit --session). Errors (return 1)
# if an explicit --session isn't a running session.
function _herdr_session_target() { … herdr session list --json | jq … ; }

# From OUTSIDE herdr, bring up a client so the just-focused workspace is visible.
# Inside herdr (HERDR_ENV set) the focus calls already switched the live client.
function _herdr_attach_if_outside() {
    [ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ] && return 0
    local session="${1:-default}"
    if [ "$session" = default ]; then herdr; else herdr session attach "$session"; fi
}
```

In **both** `herdr-vibe` and `herdr-code`:
- Parse a new `--session NAME` flag (add to the `while`/`case`, the `-h` help text, and reject empty).
- After arg parsing, resolve the session:
  ```sh
  local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
  sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
  sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}; sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
  [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
  ```
  (When inside herdr with no `--session`, `sess_sock` is empty → ambient socket is used untouched; `sess_name` is derived for the — unused — attach path.)
- **Idempotent fast path** (`existing` found): keep `herdr workspace focus "$existing"` but append `_herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"` (still gated on `--no-attach`).
- **End-of-build attach block** (`if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then …`): keep the existing `workspace focus`/`tab focus`/`pane focus` lines, add `_herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"` as the last line inside the block.
- Update each `-h` help block: document `--session NAME` and the new "attaches when run outside herdr" behavior.

No change to the reused `_sesh_*` helpers or the layout logic.
